conditions: The xsl:call-template instruction has a present focus and resolves to a named template in a valid XSLT 3.0 stylesheet.
The callee either omits xsl:context-item or declares use="absent" on that element without an as attribute.
limitations: The absent declaration must be valid. Section 10.1.1 forbids an as attribute on an xsl:context-item with use="absent".
This revision covers named-call focus only. Matching-rule dispatch, initial named-template invocation, other context-item declarations, and type or evaluation failures have separate rules.

triggers: W3C source correction or erratum, spec byte drift, or material contrary scoped evidence.

statement: In XSLT 3.0, when xsl:call-template is evaluated with a present focus, the named template’s sequence constructor inherits that focus if the template has no xsl:context-item declaration. If the template declares xsl:context-item with use="absent", its sequence constructor and any xsl:param elements are evaluated with absent focus even though the caller has a present focus.
